questions.question: Complete the sentence: My sister is ___ architect.
questions.explanation: 'Architect' begins with a vowel sound, so it takes 'an'.

questions.question: Choose the correct sentence.
questions.explanation: The 'h' in 'honest' is silent, so the word begins with a vowel sound.

questions.question: Complete the sentence: She works as ___ university lecturer.
questions.explanation: 'University' begins with the consonant sound /juː/, so it takes 'a'.

questions.question: Choose the correct sentence.
options: The Dr Rao is a professor.
A Dr Rao is a professor.
An Dr Rao is a professor.
questions.explanation: Titles such as Dr are used without an article before a person's name.

questions.question: Complete the sentence: She wants to become ___ IAS officer.
questions.explanation: The initialism 'IAS' is pronounced beginning with the vowel sound /aɪ/, so it takes 'an'.

questions.question: Choose the correct sentence.
questions.explanation: A singular countable profession normally takes an article. 'Engineer' begins with a vowel sound.

questions.question: Complete the sentence: ___ President of India addressed the gathering.
questions.explanation: The article 'the' is used with a unique official title followed by an identifying phrase.

questions.question: Which sentence is correct?
options: The Professor Mehta delivered the lecture.
A Professor Mehta delivered the lecture.
An Professor Mehta delivered the lecture.
questions.explanation: A title placed directly before a person's name normally takes no article.

questions.question: Complete the sentence: He is ___ MBA graduate.
questions.explanation: 'MBA' is pronounced beginning with the vowel sound /em/, so it takes 'an'.

questions.question: Choose the correct sentence.
options: She consulted an doctor who specialises in children.
She consulted a doctor who specialises in children.
She consulted the doctor who specialises in children, without any previous context.
She consulted doctor who specialises in children.
questions.correctAnswer: She consulted a doctor who specialises in children.
questions.explanation: The sentence introduces one unspecified doctor. 'Doctor' begins with a consonant sound.

questions.question: Complete the sentence: My brother is ___ European diplomat.
questions.explanation: 'European' begins with the consonant sound /j/, so it takes 'a'.

questions.question: Which sentence correctly uses a title before a name?
options: The Captain Sharma is in charge.
A Captain Sharma is in charge.
An Captain Sharma is in charge.
questions.explanation: A title directly before a person's name generally takes no article.

questions.question: Complete the sentence: She met ___ one-eyed scientist at the conference.
questions.explanation: 'One' begins with the consonant sound /w/, so 'a' is used.

questions.question: Choose the correct sentence.
options: The doctor who treated me was very patient.
A doctor who treated me was very patient, referring to the specific doctor already known.
Doctor who treated me was very patient.
An doctor who treated me was very patient.
questions.correctAnswer: The doctor who treated me was very patient.
questions.explanation: The identifying clause 'who treated me' points to a specific doctor, so 'the' is appropriate.
